subject: `path_type` narrows the converted value's type for `convert` and `prompt`
summary: This commit makes Path generic over the type set by `path_type`, so `convert` and `coerce_path_result` now return that type. coerce_path_result was rewritten to assign the result to a variable and cast it at the end instead of returning early. I selected the 27 tests that run Path.__init__, convert and coerce_path_result. They include the focused tests in tests/test_types/test_Path.py, such as test_path_type for str, bytes, Path and None, plus the option, argument and command tests that use Path.

risks: Most of this change is about static types (the TypeVar default and the Generic base class). Runtime tests cannot check it; that needs mypy/pyright on the typing tests.
The class-level change (new Generic base class and TypeVar) affects every Path user, but the graph only records coverage per function. Code that subscripts or subclasses Path is not tracked.
There is no record of past test runs for these functions, so no remembered failures could guide the selection.
